title: Jenkins' Orphanage bands
summary: He describes the orphanage's five or six brass bands, which played on street corners to raise money, and names Charlie Anderson and others who came from it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Another thing that I remember was [Jenkin's] Orphanage.
It was an orphanage. They had five or six bands, you know. Underprivileged kids, you know
And they all had instruments, and used to play. They used to go on corners and play on every other corner and play.
Well, you mean they were in Charleston, too?
Well, was there a Jenkin's Orphanage in alot of places?
That's where it was. In the center, Charleston is the -- as far as music is concerned, I mean, Charleston has always been musical.
Really? And they had about five different bands?

And they had about five different bands. And they could -- because they used to send them all over the city, in other words, to work on different street corners and, you know, pick up money that way to help the orphanage.
The orphanage? And they had -- so they had those instruments --
They used to come on my neighborhood, and I used to stop whatever I was doing, and follow them all over the city.
Would they be sort of marching band sort of? of thing?
Marching band, you know. Yeah. They were a marching band. But they would play the 'St. Louis Blues' and all of the -- whatever was happening during that period.
You know -- the trombone -- they were strictly a brass band, more or less.
They specialized in drums and the brass.
-- And the brass. Mr. Greene: Right. Did you ever know any -- was there anyone there blowing that you came to know afterwards?
Charlie Anderson was from the Jenkin's Orphanage? Mr. Dance: Yeah.
Yeah. There's so many -- listen, there are so many musicians who --
Like the guys before my time. I used to hear about a guy called Specs. And there's a guy -- about -- oh, so many different -- I can't think of it --
There was a trombone player they always talked of called Briscoe Do you remember him?
Yeah. I heard about him. I heard quite a bit about him.
